difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism stimulus with two premise distractors that share topic but use different forms (one adds an extra premise, one reverses the disjunct direction). Students must formalize A ∨ B; ¬A; ∴ B.
stimulus: The budget shortfall must be addressed either by raising taxes or by cutting services. The city council has ruled out raising taxes. Therefore, services must be cut.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A successful harvest requires either sufficient rainfall or irrigation. This season the farm received sufficient rainfall. Therefore, the harvest will be successful.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every patient must receive either medication or surgery to recover. This patient has not responded to medication. Therefore, this patient must receive surgery to recover.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the contract was signed before the deadline or it is invalid. Several witnesses confirm it was signed before the deadline. Therefore, the contract is probably valid.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The laboratory can produce results only if both the equipment functions and the reagents are fresh. The reagents are fresh. Therefore, the laboratory can produce results.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The defendant is either guilty of fraud or guilty of negligence. Since the defendant is guilty of fraud, the defendant is not guilty of negligence.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. Choice B matches exactly — either medication or surgery; medication has failed (not medication); therefore surgery.
explanations.A: Same-topic trap: this affirms one disjunct and concludes the broader goal is achieved, which is affirming the disjunct — a different, valid structure (sufficient condition met), not disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.B: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism: either medication or surgery; not medication; therefore surgery.
explanations.C: Strength-shift trap: the conclusion says 'probably valid' rather than 'must be valid,' weakening the modal force relative to the stimulus.
explanations.D: Wrong form: this is a conjunction stimulus (both P and Q required), not a disjunction. Only one conjunct is confirmed, making the conclusion actually invalid — a form mismatch.
explanations.E: Same structure inverted: this affirms one disjunct and denies the other, which is the fallacy of affirming a disjunct, not disjunctive syllogism.

difficultyReason: Contrapositive stimulus (modus tollens) with distractors that use modus ponens or affirm the consequent — students must distinguish direction of the conditional.
stimulus: If a species is highly specialized, it will struggle when its environment changes. The Arctic fox has not struggled as its environment has changed. Therefore, the Arctic fox is not highly specialized.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a contract is enforceable, it must include consideration. This contract includes consideration. Therefore, this contract is enforceable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a new technology is widely adopted, it must be affordable. This technology has not been widely adopted. Therefore, this technology is not affordable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a painting is by Rembrandt, it will display chiaroscuro. This painting does not display chiaroscuro. Therefore, this painting is not by Rembrandt.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a student studies diligently, the student will pass the examination. This student studied diligently. Therefore, this student will pass the examination.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a metal is exposed to moisture, it will corrode. This metal has corroded. Therefore, this metal was exposed to moisture.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P (modus tollens / contrapositive). Choice C: If Rembrandt then chiaroscuro; no chiaroscuro; therefore not Rembrandt — identical form.
explanations.A: Affirming the consequent fallacy: if P then Q; Q; therefore P. This is invalid and structurally opposite in direction to modus tollens.
explanations.B: Denying the antecedent fallacy: if P then Q; not P; therefore not Q. This is a common trap — the negation is in the wrong position.
explanations.C: Correct. Modus tollens: If Rembrandt → chiaroscuro; not chiaroscuro; therefore not Rembrandt.
explanations.D: Modus ponens: if P then Q; P; therefore Q. Different valid form — affirms the antecedent rather than denying the consequent.
explanations.E: Affirming the consequent: if exposure then corrosion; corrosion occurred; therefore exposure. Invalid form, structurally distinct from modus tollens.

difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular (categorical syllogism: All A are B; x is A; ∴ x is B) with distractors using 'most' or 'some' to create strength-shift traps.
stimulus: Every regulation passed by the legislature that conflicts with the constitution is invalid. The emergency housing decree conflicts with the constitution. Therefore, the emergency housing decree is invalid.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most medications that interact with anticoagulants are contraindicated for post-operative patients. This antibiotic interacts with anticoagulants. Therefore, this antibiotic is probably contraindicated for post-operative patients.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every metal that conducts electricity can be used in circuit boards. Copper conducts electricity. Therefore, copper can be used in circuit boards.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some tax shelters that exploit offshore accounts are illegal. This investment scheme exploits offshore accounts. Therefore, this investment scheme is illegal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No language that lacks written records can be fully reconstructed. Ancient Elamite lacks written records. Therefore, Ancient Elamite cannot be fully reconstructed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every employee who meets the performance benchmarks receives a bonus. Several employees received bonuses last quarter. Therefore, those employees met the performance benchmarks.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B. Choice B matches: all metals that conduct electricity can be used in circuit boards; copper conducts electricity; therefore copper can be used in circuit boards.
explanations.A: Strength-shift trap: uses 'most' instead of 'every,' downgrading the universal quantifier, making the conclusion only probable rather than certain.
explanations.B: Correct. All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B — perfect universal-to-particular match.
explanations.C: Quantifier trap: 'some A are B; x is A; therefore x is B' is an invalid inference. The existential 'some' does not support a particular conclusion about x.
explanations.D: Same-premise-count but different form: 'No A can B; x is A; therefore x cannot B' — this is a universal negative syllogism (celarent), structurally distinct from the affirmative universal in the stimulus.
explanations.E: Affirming the consequent in categorical form: All A are B; x is B; therefore x is A — the direction is reversed.

difficultyReason: Conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C) with distractors that interrupt the chain or use the chain without affirming the antecedent.
stimulus: Whenever inflation rises sharply, consumer confidence falls. Whenever consumer confidence falls, retail sales decline. Inflation has risen sharply. Therefore, retail sales will decline.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever a forest fire occurs, air quality deteriorates. Whenever air quality deteriorates, respiratory illness rates rise. A forest fire has occurred. Therefore, respiratory illness rates will rise.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a diplomat is recalled, tensions between nations increase. If tensions between nations increase, trade is disrupted. Trade has been disrupted. Therefore, a diplomat was recalled.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever drought conditions persist, crop yields fall. Crop yields have fallen in the northern region. Therefore, drought conditions must have persisted in the northern region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a software update is released, users must restart their devices. If users restart their devices, unsaved work is lost. A software update was released. Therefore, unsaved work may be lost.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whenever interest rates rise, borrowing costs increase. Whenever borrowing costs increase, housing starts fall. Interest rates have not risen. Therefore, housing starts will not fall.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C. Choice A matches exactly: fire → air quality deteriorates → illness rises; fire occurred; therefore illness rises.
explanations.A: Correct. Three-premise conditional chain with antecedent affirmed — identical structure.
explanations.B: Affirming the consequent in the chain: presents A → B; B → C; C; therefore A — the consequent is affirmed to reach the antecedent, which is an invalid form.
explanations.C: This is a two-premise modus tollens chain variant: only one conditional; and the conclusion is reached by affirming the consequent, making it invalid — both count and form diverge.
explanations.D: Strength-shift trap: conclusion says 'may be lost' rather than 'will be lost,' weakening the modal force despite having the correct chain structure.
explanations.E: Denying the antecedent fallacy: A → B; B → C; ¬A; ∴ ¬C. The negation is applied to the antecedent, not the consequent.

difficultyReason: Analogy stimulus (X resembles Y in two key respects; Y has property R; ∴ X has R) with distractors that use only one respect or reverse the direction of analogy.
stimulus: The new compound shares with penicillin both its molecular ring structure and its mechanism of disrupting bacterial cell walls. Penicillin is effective against streptococcal infections. Therefore, the new compound is likely effective against streptococcal infections.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This bridge design shares with the Golden Gate Bridge both its cable suspension system and its load-distribution geometry. The Golden Gate Bridge has withstood major seismic events. Therefore, this bridge design will likely withstand major seismic events.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This sculpture is made of marble and depicts a reclining figure. Most classical sculptures depict reclining figures. Therefore, this sculpture is probably classical.

choices.label: C
choices.text: This vineyard has the same altitude and rainfall as a celebrated Burgundy vineyard. Wine from the Burgundy vineyard ages well. Therefore, wine from this vineyard will certainly age well.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new fuel cell shares its hydrogen-oxidation mechanism with conventional batteries. Conventional batteries power electric vehicles effectively. Therefore, the new fuel cell is probably a type of conventional battery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: This novel and the prize-winning novel both explore themes of exile and memory. Therefore, this novel will probably win a prize.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: X shares two properties with Y; Y has result R; therefore X likely has R. Choice A: new bridge shares two structural features with Golden Gate; Golden Gate withstands seismic events; therefore new bridge will likely do so.
explanations.A: Correct. Two shared respects established, then a property of the analogue is transferred to the subject via 'likely' — exact structural match.
explanations.B: Same-topic trap plus base-rate reversal: notes one shared feature and then reasons backward from a general pattern to classify the particular item, which is a different form.
explanations.C: Strength-shift trap: the conclusion uses 'certainly' rather than 'likely,' escalating the modal force beyond what the analogical form supports.
explanations.D: Conclusion-type mismatch: the conclusion classifies the subject as a type of the analogue ('is a type of conventional battery') rather than attributing a property to it — different logical goal.
explanations.E: Premise-count trap: only one shared property (theme) is noted, and the analogue's prize-winning is presupposed rather than stated as a premise, making the structure deficient.

difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism with three answer-choice traps: one extra premise, one affirms a disjunct, one uses a conjunction instead of disjunction. Students must identify A ∨ B; ¬B; ∴ A.
stimulus: The manuscript was written either in the fourteenth century or in the fifteenth century. Paleographic analysis has established that it was not written in the fifteenth century. Therefore, the manuscript was written in the fourteenth century.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volcanic eruption originated either from a shallow magma chamber or from a deep mantle plume. Seismic data confirm it originated from a deep mantle plume. Therefore, it did not originate from a shallow magma chamber.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The artifact was produced either by the Minoan civilization or by the Mycenaean civilization. Isotope analysis rules out Mycenaean origin. Therefore, the artifact was produced by the Minoan civilization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The policy failure resulted either from poor planning, from inadequate funding, or from weak enforcement. Investigators have ruled out poor planning and inadequate funding. Therefore, the failure resulted from weak enforcement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The signal was transmitted either by satellite or by fiber optic cable, and it was encrypted. The signal was transmitted by satellite. Therefore, the signal was encrypted and transmitted by satellite.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The theorem was proved either by induction or by contradiction. Since the proof used contradiction, the theorem is valid.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; not B; therefore A. Choice B: Minoan or Mycenaean; not Mycenaean; therefore Minoan — perfect disjunctive syllogism match with two disjuncts.
explanations.A: Affirms one disjunct and denies the other — the opposite direction. The conclusion denies rather than affirms the remaining option, though the form is the fallacy of affirming a disjunct.
explanations.B: Correct. Two-disjunct disjunctive syllogism with the second disjunct eliminated.
explanations.C: Premise-count trap: this is a three-disjunct version, requiring two eliminations before concluding. The structure has an extra elimination step not present in the stimulus.
explanations.D: Conjunction trap: introduces an independent conjunct ('and it was encrypted') that makes the premise structure a conjunction with a disjunction, not a simple disjunction.
explanations.E: Conclusion-type mismatch: the conclusion ('the theorem is valid') does not follow from which proof method was used — the reasoning introduces an unsupported claim, making it invalid and structurally mismatched.

difficultyReason: Modus tollens (contrapositive) stimulus in an ethics domain; distractors use modus ponens, denying the antecedent, or affirming the consequent — students must track conditional direction carefully.
stimulus: Any action that violates a person's autonomy without consent is morally impermissible. The proposed surveillance program does not violate anyone's autonomy without consent. Therefore, the proposed surveillance program is not morally impermissible on those grounds.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any ingredient that triggers an allergic reaction in a patient must be excluded from the formulation. Casein triggers an allergic reaction in this patient. Therefore, casein must be excluded from the formulation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any construction project that exceeds its budget is subject to a compliance review. This project has not exceeded its budget. Therefore, this project is not subject to a compliance review on those grounds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any judicial ruling that contradicts precedent must be reviewed by the appellate court. This ruling has been reviewed by the appellate court. Therefore, this ruling contradicted precedent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any policy that reduces greenhouse gas emissions should be adopted. The carbon tax reduces greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, the carbon tax should be adopted.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any artist who does not submit work by the deadline is disqualified. This artist has been disqualified. Therefore, this artist did not submit work by the deadline.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A are B (impermissible); x is not A (does not violate autonomy without consent); therefore x is not B (not impermissible) — modus tollens on the universal: denying membership in the trigger class to deny membership in the consequence class.
explanations.A: Modus ponens: All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B — affirms the antecedent rather than denying it.
explanations.B: Correct. All A are B; x is not A; therefore x is not B — same form as the stimulus, denying the antecedent class to deny the consequent class (valid here because 'any' makes B conditional solely on A).
explanations.C: Affirming the consequent in categorical form: All A must B; x did B; therefore x is A — invalid and directionally reversed.
explanations.D: Modus ponens: All A should be adopted; x is A; therefore x should be adopted — correct form is different (antecedent affirmed).
explanations.E: Affirming the consequent: All not-submit are disqualified; x is disqualified; therefore x did not submit — reversed conditional direction.

difficultyReason: Conditional chain where the antecedent is negated at the conclusion step; tests whether students can track a two-step chain and correctly apply the affirmed antecedent, with distractors that break the chain or shift strength.
stimulus: Whenever a river's sediment load increases, its delta expands. Whenever a delta expands, coastal wetlands are displaced. The sediment load of the Nile River has increased. Therefore, coastal wetlands along the Nile will be displaced.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever a government subsidizes an industry, domestic production rises. Whenever domestic production rises, import reliance falls. The government has subsidized the steel industry. Therefore, import reliance in steel will fall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whenever a central bank raises interest rates, borrowing slows. Borrowing has slowed in the current economy. Therefore, the central bank has raised interest rates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever a language loses native speakers, it becomes endangered. Whenever it becomes endangered, preservation efforts increase. Preservation efforts for Cornish have increased. Therefore, Cornish has lost native speakers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whenever a composer writes in a minor key, the piece evokes melancholy. This piece evokes melancholy. Therefore, the composer wrote it in a minor key.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whenever a drought occurs, water restrictions are imposed. Water restrictions have not been imposed in this region. Therefore, a drought has not occurred in this region.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C. Choice A: subsidy → production rises → import reliance falls; subsidy occurred; therefore import reliance falls — identical three-premise conditional chain.
explanations.A: Correct. Two conditionals chained, antecedent of the first affirmed, conclusion is the consequent of the second.
explanations.B: Affirming the consequent: A → B; B; therefore A. Only one conditional used, and the direction is reversed.
explanations.C: Affirming the consequent at the end of a chain: A → B; B → C; C; therefore A — the chain runs backward from the final consequent.
explanations.D: Single conditional with affirming the consequent: A → B; B; therefore A. Both premise count and direction mismatch.
explanations.E: Modus tollens on a single conditional: A → B; ¬B; therefore ¬A. Only one premise and uses contrapositive, not chain.

difficultyReason: Universal negative syllogism (No A are B; x is A; ∴ x is not B) with distractors using affirmative universals, strength-softening, or reversed quantifiers.
stimulus: No algorithm that relies solely on historical data can accurately predict unprecedented market events. The firm's trading algorithm relies solely on historical data. Therefore, the firm's trading algorithm cannot accurately predict unprecedented market events.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No surgical procedure performed without informed consent is ethically permissible. This procedure was performed without informed consent. Therefore, this procedure is not ethically permissible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most diagnostic tests that rely on a single biomarker are unreliable. This test relies on a single biomarker. Therefore, this test is probably unreliable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No poem written in strict meter can capture the randomness of spoken language. This poem does not capture the randomness of spoken language. Therefore, this poem was written in strict meter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All governance frameworks that lack independent oversight are prone to corruption. This framework lacks independent oversight. Therefore, this framework is prone to corruption.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some investment strategies that ignore macroeconomic trends produce poor returns. This strategy ignores macroeconomic trends. Therefore, this strategy will produce poor returns.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: No A are B; x is A; therefore x is not B. Choice A: No consent-free procedure is ethically permissible; this procedure lacks consent; therefore it is not permissible — identical universal negative syllogism.
explanations.A: Correct. Universal negative premise + singular affirming the subject category = singular negative conclusion.
explanations.B: Quantifier-shift trap: uses 'most' instead of 'no,' reducing the universal negative to a probabilistic claim and softening the conclusion to 'probably.'
explanations.C: Affirming the consequent of a universal negative in categorical form: No A is B; x is not B; therefore x is A — reversed direction, invalid.
explanations.D: Affirmative universal trap: 'All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B' — the premise is affirmative, not negative, giving a structurally distinct syllogism.
explanations.E: Existential quantifier trap: 'Some A are B; x is A; therefore x is B' — an invalid inference from 'some,' mismatching both quantifier type and validity.

difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism combined with a conditional conclusion (A ∨ B; ¬A; B → C; ∴ C) slightly extending the standard two-premise form; distractors omit one step or reverse the elimination.
stimulus: The exhibit was funded either through private donations or through a government grant. It was not funded through private donations. Any exhibit funded through a government grant is subject to public audit. Therefore, the exhibit is subject to public audit.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The suspect traveled either by train or by car. The suspect traveled by train. Any suspect who travels by train passes through a monitored station. Therefore, the suspect passed through a monitored station.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The package was shipped either by air or by sea. It was not shipped by air. Any package shipped by sea is subject to customs inspection. Therefore, the package is subject to customs inspection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The grant was awarded either for research or for outreach. It was awarded for research. Research grants require annual reporting. Outreach grants do not require annual reporting. Therefore, this grant requires annual reporting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The building was designed either by a licensed architect or by an unlicensed contractor. Any building designed by an unlicensed contractor is a code violation. Therefore, the building may be a code violation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The film was screened either at a festival or at a commercial venue. It was not screened at a festival. Commercial venues charge admission fees. Therefore, the film probably generated revenue.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A ∨ B; ¬A; therefore B; B → C; therefore C — disjunctive syllogism feeding a conditional. Choice B: air or sea; not air; therefore sea; sea → customs inspection; therefore customs inspection. Exact three-premise match.
explanations.A: Affirms rather than eliminates a disjunct: 'traveled by train' is asserted directly (not via elimination of the other disjunct), so the disjunctive syllogism step is absent.
explanations.B: Correct. Eliminates one disjunct (not air), derives the other (sea), then applies the conditional (sea → customs) to reach the conclusion.
explanations.C: Premise-count and conclusion-type trap: adds an extra contrasting conditional for outreach (not in the stimulus structure) and includes an irrelevant fourth premise, making it a more complex argument form.
explanations.D: Missing elimination step: the disjunction is stated but neither disjunct is eliminated — the argument leaps directly to a weakened probable conclusion without completing the disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Strength-shift and conclusion-mismatch: conclusion is 'probably generated revenue' rather than the direct consequence required by the structure, and 'generated revenue' is not the direct consequent of 'commercial venue' but an additional inference.
